_about: Doña Rosario, a hammock weaver, and Pepe the iguana at the ruins (x08-rosario, a bonus chat).

items.prompt: Doña Rosario sits on the stone bench in the shade about one third from the left, the half-woven striped hammock in her lap and a wooden weaving needle in one hand, raising the other hand in a friendly greeting with a warm smile. Pepe, the big green iguana, basks on his sunny stone to the right of her.
Change only her pose and what she holds: she fans herself with a woven palm-leaf fan, looking up at the bright sky with a comic, long-suffering face: so hot today!
Change only her pose: she pats the shady stone bench beside her with one hand and smiles knowingly: here in the shade it's better.
Change only her pose: she points with an amused, proud smile at Pepe the iguana on his stone, who lifts his head like a little king.

A close view of Pepe, a big green iguana with a spiny crest and a round dewlap, lying stretched out with his eyes half closed on a flat, warm block of pale stone in full sun, utterly content; the sunny lawn and the old wall soft behind him. Nobody is in the picture.
Change only her pose: she laughs and waves one hand dismissively, reassuring the learner; Pepe sleeps peacefully: he's harmless.
Change only her pose and what she holds: she leans toward Pepe and holds out a slice of ripe orange mango to him on her open palm; he stretches his head toward it.
Change only her pose: she holds up the half-woven hammock with both hands to show its bright rainbow stripes, smiling proudly: it's for her grandson.
Change only her pose: she smiles warmly and gestures with an open hand to the free place on the bench beside her, inviting the learner to sit, then to come back whenever they like.
